title: Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech's” — how did the land come to be hers to sell?
summary: Boaz tells the nearer kinsman that Naomi “selleth a parcel of land” that was Elimelech’s, and afterwards says he has bought all that was Elimelech’s, Chilion’s and Mahlon’s “of the hand of Naomi”. The order of inheritance given in Numbers 27:8–11 names a son, a daughter, brethren, the father’s brethren and the nearest kinsman. The verses compared do not say how the land came into Naomi’s hand, or what exactly she was selling.
text: KJV Ruth 1:3: “And Elimelech Naomi's husband died; and she was left, and her two sons.” KJV 1:5: “And Mahlon and Chilion died also both of them; and the woman was left of her two sons and her husband.” KJV 4:3: “And he said unto the kinsman, Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech's:” KJV 4:5: “What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead” KJV 4:9: “And Boaz said unto the elders, and unto all the people, Ye are witnesses this day, that I have bought all that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, of the hand of Naomi.” KJV Numbers 27:8: “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter” KJV 27:9: “And if he have no daughter, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his brethren.” KJV 27:10: “And if he have no brethren, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his father's brethren.” KJV 27:11: “And if his father have no brethren, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his kinsman that is next to him of his family, and he shall possess it” KJV Leviticus 25:25: “If thy brother be waxen poor, and hath sold away some of his possession, and if any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold.” KJV 2 Kings 8:3: “she went forth to cry unto the king for her house and for her land” KJV 8:6: “Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now” Hebrew (WLC) Ruth 4:3: חֶלְקַת֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאָחִ֖ינוּ לֶאֱלִימֶ֑לֶךְ מָכְרָ֣ה נָעֳמִ֔י [the portion of the field that was our brother Elimelech's, Naomi has sold, or sells]. 4:9: מִיַּ֖ד נָעֳמִֽי [from the hand of Naomi]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ruth 4:3: τὴν μερίδα τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἥ ἐστι τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ ἡμῶν τοῦ Ἐλιμέλεχ, ἣ δέδοται Νωεμὶν [the portion of the field which is our brother Elimelech's, which has been given to Naomi]. 4:9: ἐκ χειρὸς Νωεμίν [from the hand of Naomi]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/8/4/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/RUT04.htm.
reasoning: The sale is the business Boaz brings to the gate: it is what he puts to the nearer kinsman, and what he afterwards says he has bought. Elimelech and both his sons are dead (1:3, 1:5), and the land is spoken of as Elimelech’s, Chilion’s and Mahlon’s, yet it passes “of the hand of Naomi”. The order of inheritance quoted from Numbers passes a dead man’s inheritance to a son, a daughter, his brethren, his father’s brethren and then his nearest kinsman; those four verses do not name his widow. How Naomi held the land decides what the redeemer was acquiring from her — the field itself, the use of it, or a right over land already in another’s hands — and bears on why Ruth is joined to the purchase at 4:5.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. Readings that have been proposed, none of which the verses quoted state: that a widow kept her husband’s land for her lifetime, or until an heir was raised, by a custom not written in the laws quoted; that the land had passed out of the family’s hands when they went to Moab and what Naomi offers is the right to redeem it, the case Leviticus 25:25 speaks of; that the land was assigned to Naomi, as the Greek quoted says it “has been given” to her. Limits: Numbers 27:8–11 is given in answer to a case about daughters and does not say that its order is the only way land could be held, so its not naming a widow is not a statement that a widow could hold nothing; 2 Kings 8:3 and 8:6 speak of a woman’s house and land as “hers” and are quoted to show that wording, and they do not say how she held them or that her case was like Naomi’s; the Hebrew verb at 4:3 is a form usually rendered as past and can also state an act done in the speaking, and the verses quoted do not say whether a sale had already been made; the Greek “has been given” differs from the KJV’s “selleth” and that difference is not examined here. Check made: a whole-word search of the packaged KJV for “Elimelech” finds Ruth 1:2, 1:3, 2:1, 2:3, 4:3 and 4:9 only; Ruth 1–4 was read in the KJV, with Numbers 27:1–11, Leviticus 25:25 and 2 Kings 8:3 and 8:6; Ruth 4:3 and 4:9 were also read in the Hebrew and the Greek. That is a word search and a reading of those verses, not a reading of the whole Bible. These checked verses do not explicitly settle how the land came to be Naomi’s to sell. No H or G is proposed. title: By what law or custom did redeeming Elimelech’s field carry the duty “to raise up the name of the dead” through Ruth?
summary: The nearer kinsman agrees to redeem the field. Boaz then joins Ruth, “the wife of the dead”, to the purchase, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance”, and the kinsman withdraws. The law of redemption quoted from Leviticus speaks of land, and the law quoted from Deuteronomy speaks of a husband’s brother. The verses compared do not say what joined the two duties in a kinsman who is not called the dead man’s brother.
text: KJV Ruth 2:1: “a kinsman of her husband's, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech” KJV 2:20: “The man is near of kin unto us, one of our next kinsmen” KJV 3:9: “spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman” KJV 3:13: “if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman's part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to thee, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee” KJV 4:3: “which was our brother Elimelech” KJV 4:4: “And he said, I will redeem it.” KJV 4:5: “Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.” KJV 4:6: “And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself; for I cannot redeem it.” KJV 4:10: “Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance” KJV Leviticus 25:25: “If thy brother be waxen poor, and hath sold away some of his possession, and if any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold.” KJV Deuteronomy 25:5: “If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband's brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband's brother unto her.” KJV 25:6: “And it shall be, that the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.” KJV 25:7: “My husband's brother refuseth to raise up unto his brother a name in Israel” KJV Genesis 38:8: “And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother.” Hebrew (WLC) Ruth 3:9: כִּ֥י גֹאֵ֖ל אָֽתָּה [for thou art a redeemer]. 4:5: לְהָקִ֥ים שֵׁם־הַמֵּ֖ת עַל־נַחֲלָתֹֽו [to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance]. Leviticus 25:25: וּבָ֤א גֹֽאֲלֹו֙ הַקָּרֹ֣ב אֵלָ֔יו [and his redeemer who is near to him comes]. Deuteronomy 25:5: יְבָמָהּ֙ יָבֹ֣א עָלֶ֔יהָ [her husband's brother shall go in unto her]. 25:7: לְהָקִ֨ים לְאָחִ֥יו שֵׁם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל [to raise up for his brother a name in Israel]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ruth 3:9: ὅτι ἀγχιστεὺς εἶ σύ [for thou art a near kinsman]. 4:5: καὶ αὐτὴν κτήσασθαί σε δεῖ, ὥστε ἀναστῆσαι τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ τεθνηκότος ἐπὶ τῆς κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ [thou must acquire her also, so as to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance]. Deuteronomy 25:5: ὁ ἀδελφὸς τοῦ ἀνδρὸς αὐτῆς εἰσελεύσεται πρὸς αὐτὴν [the brother of her husband shall go in to her]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/8/3/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/8/4/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/3/25/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/5/25/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/RUT03.htm, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/RUT04.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/DEU25.htm.
reasoning: The story turns on this link. The nearer kinsman says “I will redeem it” while only the field is named (4:4), and says “I cannot redeem it” once Ruth and the name of the dead are joined to it (4:5–6). Leviticus 25:25 speaks of a kinsman redeeming what was sold, and that verse says nothing of a widow. Deuteronomy 25:5–7 speaks of “brethren” who “dwell together” and of the “husband's brother” taking the widow. Boaz is called a kinsman of Naomi’s husband, “of the family of Elimelech” (2:1), and calls Elimelech “our brother” (4:3); the verses quoted do not call Boaz or the nearer kinsman a brother of Mahlon. The passage does not state the rule under which a redeemer of the land took on the dead man’s name, or whether the nearer kinsman was bound by it or free to decline.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. Readings that have been proposed, none of which the verses quoted state: that the duty of Deuteronomy 25:5–10 was understood to fall on the nearest kinsman when no husband’s brother was living, “brethren” being taken widely as Boaz’s “our brother” at 4:3 may be; that there was a custom of the redeemer wider than either law quoted, covering the land and the widow together; that no law bound either man to take Ruth, and Boaz, who had promised Ruth to act (3:13), made her part of the matter he put to the kinsman. Limits: the Hebrew of Ruth 3:9 and 4:5 uses the word for a redeemer that stands in Leviticus 25:25 and the phrase for raising up a name that stands in Deuteronomy 25:7, but shared words do not settle that the same law is being applied; the Hebrew word for a husband’s brother that stands in Deuteronomy 25:5 and 25:7 is not in the Hebrew of the nine Ruth verses quoted here from chapters 2 to 4; a law need not list every case it was applied to; in the KJV of 4:5 the kinsman must buy the field “of Ruth”, and the marriage is stated in Boaz’s own words at 4:10, while the Greek quoted at 4:5 speaks of acquiring her, and the Hebrew verse carries a written and a read form of the verb — these differences of wording are noted and not examined here; Genesis 38:8 tells of a brother, before the law was given, and says nothing of land. Check made: a whole-word search of the packaged KJV for “husband's brother” finds Deuteronomy 25:5 and 25:7 only, and for “name of the dead” finds Ruth 4:5 and 4:10 only; Ruth 1–4 was read in the KJV, with Leviticus 25:25, Deuteronomy 25:5–10 and Genesis 38:8. That is a word search and a reading of those verses, not a reading of the whole Bible. These checked verses do not explicitly settle what joined the two duties. No H, G or V is proposed. title: Boaz took Ruth “to raise up the name of the dead”, and “Boaz begat Obed” — in whose line was the child counted, and how was the dead man’s name raised?
summary: Boaz says he takes Ruth “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off”. When the child is born the women say, “There is a son born to Naomi”, and the list that closes the book says “Boaz begat Obed”. The verses compared give Obed as the son of Boaz and do not name Mahlon or Elimelech in the line; they do not say how the name of the dead was raised up.
text: KJV Ruth 4:5: “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance” KJV 4:10: “Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place: ye are witnesses this day.” KJV 4:13: “So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.” KJV 4:16: “And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it.” KJV 4:17: “And the women her neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.” KJV 4:21: “And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,” KJV 4:22: “And Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.” KJV Deuteronomy 25:6: “And it shall be, that the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.” KJV 1 Chronicles 2:12: “And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse,” KJV Matthew 1:5: “and Booz begat Obed of Ruth” KJV Luke 3:32: “which was the son of Obed, which was the son of Booz” Hebrew (WLC) Ruth 4:10: לְהָקִ֤ים שֵׁם־הַמֵּת֙ עַל־נַ֣חֲלָתֹ֔ו וְלֹא־יִכָּרֵ֧ת שֵׁם־הַמֵּ֛ת מֵעִ֥ם אֶחָ֖יו [to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, and the name of the dead shall not be cut off from among his brethren]. 4:17: יֻלַּד־בֵּ֖ן לְנָעֳמִ֑י [a son has been born to Naomi]. 4:21: וּבֹ֖עַז הֹולִ֥יד אֶת־עֹובֵֽד [and Boaz begat Obed]. 1 Chronicles 2:12: וּבֹ֙עַז֙ הֹולִ֣יד אֶת־עֹובֵ֔ד [and Boaz begat Obed]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ruth 4:10: τοῦ ἀναστῆσαι τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ τεθνηκότος ἐπὶ τῆς κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ [to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance]. 4:17: ἐτέχθη υἱὸς τῇ Νωεμίν [a son has been born to Naomi]. 4:21: καὶ Βοὸζ ἐγέννησε τὸν Ὠβήδ [and Boaz begat Obed]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/8/4/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/2/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/RUT04.htm.
reasoning: The purpose is stated twice, at 4:5 and 4:10, and it is the ground Boaz gives for the marriage before the witnesses. Deuteronomy 25:6 says of the case it covers that the firstborn “shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead”. Yet after 4:10 the book does not name Mahlon again: the women speak of a son born to Naomi, and the list of 4:18–22 runs from Salmon to Boaz to Obed. The same descent stands in 1 Chronicles 2:12, Matthew 1:5 and Luke 3:32. The book ends on David (4:17, 4:22), so the reckoning of Obed decides through whose house David’s descent is traced in it, and the verses quoted do not say what, if anything, was done to carry on the name of the dead.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. Readings that have been proposed, none of which the verses quoted state: that the name of the dead was raised “upon his inheritance” by the land remaining under his name, while descent was reckoned by the father who begat; that Obed was counted in law as the dead man’s son, which “a son born to Naomi” would fit, while the lists record the natural father; that the list of 4:18–22 is a separate record of David’s descent joined to the story and follows its own reckoning. Limits: the verses quoted do not define what raising up a name consists of; Deuteronomy 25:6 speaks of a husband’s brother, and it is not shown here that the law applied to Boaz; the women’s words may be a saying about Naomi’s joy and care for the child (4:16) and need not be a statement of legal descent; a list of who begat whom does not say that it is the only way a son was reckoned. Check made: a whole-word search of the packaged KJV for “Mahlon” finds Ruth 1:2, 1:5, 4:9 and 4:10 only, and for “Elimelech” finds Ruth 1:2, 1:3, 2:1, 2:3, 4:3 and 4:9 only; Ruth 1–4 was read in the KJV, with Deuteronomy 25:5–10, 1 Chronicles 2:11–12, Matthew 1:5 and Luke 3:32; the Greek of Matthew and Luke was not consulted. That is a word search and a reading of those verses, not a reading of the whole Bible. These checked verses do not explicitly settle in whose line Obed was counted or how the name was raised.
